conventions.convention: Standard modular data require Choice, a concrete von Neumann algebra, and a unit vector that is both cyclic and separating. The Tomita operator is the graph closure of S₀(xΩ)=x*Ω.
Hilbert inner products are linear in the first argument; proofs using (u|v) define it as ⟨v,u⟩, linear in the second argument.

The upper-strip condition has lower boundary ω(Aαₜ(B)) and upper boundary ω(αₜ(B)A), with positive dimensionless strip width β. Continuity of the automorphism group is point-ultraweak continuity against the quotient trace-class predual.
The modular flow is σₜ(x)=ΔⁱᵗxΔ⁻ⁱᵗ. Its upper-strip width-one KMS flow is αₜ=σ₋ₜ.
For a faithful Gibbs matrix, physical time satisfies αₛ=σ₋ₛ/₍βℏ₎. Here s is in seconds, β in inverse joules, ℏ in joule-seconds, and the physical-time strip width is βℏ seconds.
The resolvent parameter satisfies |λ|=1 and λ≠−1; writing λ=eⁱθ uses −π<θ<π. Spectral cutoffs are Eₙ=1_[1/n,n](Δ), n≥1.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Choice and standard modular data for a concrete von Neumann algebra with unit cyclic-separating vector Ω. For |λ|=1, λ≠−1, (Δ+λ)⁻¹M′Ω⊆MΩ. Moreover JMJ=M′, ΔⁱᵗMΔ⁻ⁱᵗ=M for every real t, and the graph closure of F₀(x′Ω)=x′*Ω is F=S*.

Under Choice and unit cyclic-separating hypotheses, S is a densely defined closed antilinear involution with S=JΔ¹ᐟ², J antiunitary, Δ positive self-adjoint and injective, J=J*=J⁻¹, JΔJ=Δ⁻¹, JΔⁱᵗJ=Δⁱᵗ, F=S*=JΔ⁻¹ᐟ²=Δ¹ᐟ²J, JΩ=Ω, and ΔΩ=Ω.

Under Choice and standard modular data for a concrete von Neumann algebra with unit cyclic-separating vector, σₜ restricts to a point-ultraweakly continuous group of normal *-automorphisms, JMJ=M′, and the vector state is faithful, normal, and upper-strip (α,1) KMS for αₜ=σ₋ₜ.

Assume Choice. For self-adjoint A with spectral measure supported on (0,∞) and ξ∈D(A¹ᐟ²), A⁻ⁱᶻ/²ξ is defined and strongly continuous on 0≤Im z≤1, has squared norm at most ‖ξ‖²+‖A¹ᐟ²ξ‖², and is norm-holomorphic in the open strip.

For a positive-definite trace-one matrix ρ acting by left multiplication on Hilbert-Schmidt matrices with Ω=ρ¹ᐟ², JX=X*, ΔX=ρXρ⁻¹, σₜ(A)=ρⁱᵗAρ⁻ⁱᵗ, and ω(A)=Tr(ρA). For ρ=e⁻ᵝᴴ/Z and αₛ(A)=eⁱˢᴴ/ℏAe⁻ⁱˢᴴ/ℏ, αₛ=σ₋ₛ/₍βℏ₎ and ω satisfies physical-time β-KMS with strip width βℏ.

alerts.finding: Proof step 3.1 says 'The function f is holomorphic on Ω\A', but step 1.1 defines A only as the poles having nonzero winding number. Other poles can remain in Ω\A. For example, take Ω=C, f(z)=1/z+1/(z−2), and Γ the positively oriented circle |z|=1/2. Then A={0}, while f still has a pole at 2 in Ω\A. Thus the stated holomorphy premise for the homology argument is false in the theorem's generality. The batch's single-pole rectangle applications do not encounter this extra-pole case.

seams_checked.note: Checked both supplier interfaces and their consuming uses: concrete closure conventions, cyclic/separating duality, antilinear adjoints and graph closure, polar decomposition, trace-class duality, and quotient predual. Choice and pairing conventions are retained. The modular proof establishes commutant equality and modular invariance locally rather than assuming them from the prerequisite page.

The rescaling lemma uses the exact upper-strip W*-KMS definition. The wedge postulate explicitly supplies a unit cyclic-separating vacuum and separately adopts Δ_Wⁱᵗ=U(Λ_W(−2πt)). The clock theorem faithfully uses αₜ=σ₋ₜ and positive rescaling to obtain width 2πc/a seconds. It preserves point-ultraweak continuity and makes no detector, density-matrix, or empirical-temperature conclusion.
